title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 10
description: Ten questions on Romans 10: zeal without knowledge, the word of faith in mouth and heart, and the need for preachers to be sent.

questions.text: For whom is the writer's heart's desire and prayer to God?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:1 says his heart's desire and his prayer to God is for Israel, that they may be saved.

answers.text: The rulers of Rome
The households of Corinth
The assemblies of Macedonia
Israel

questions.text: The writer testifies that they have a zeal for God, but not according to what?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:2 says he testifies about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

answers.text: Love
Patience
Knowledge
Custom

questions.text: To whom is Christ the fulfillment of the law for righteousness?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:4 says Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

answers.text: To the priests only
To everyone who believes
To those who were born Israelites
To those who keep every feast

questions.text: What does Moses write about the righteousness of the law?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:5 says Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, “The one who does them will live by them.”

answers.text: “The one who does them will live by them.”
“The one who hears them will be wise.”
“No one can keep them all.”
“They were written for another age.”

questions.text: Where is the word, according to the righteousness which is of faith?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:8 says the word is near you, in your mouth, and in your heart, and calls it the word of faith which we preach.

answers.text: In heaven above, beyond the reach of men
In the abyss below, among the dead
Written on the gates of the city
Near you, in your mouth and in your heart

questions.text: What does the text say brings salvation when confessed and believed?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:9 says that if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

answers.text: That the law is holy and righteous and good
That Moses was a true prophet of God
That Jesus is Lord and that God raised him from the dead
That the Scriptures were written for our learning

questions.text: Between whom does the text say there is no distinction?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:12 says there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same Lord is Lord of all and is rich to all who call on him.

answers.text: Rich and poor
Jew and Greek
Slave and free
Weak and strong

questions.text: Whose feet are called beautiful in the quotation?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:15 quotes, “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

answers.text: Those who preach the Good News of peace
Those who go up to the temple
Those who run in the race
Those who keep watch at night

questions.text: How does faith come, according to the text?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:17 says faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

answers.text: By works of the law and its ordinances
By signs and wonders done among the nations
By the wisdom of men and persuasive words
By hearing, and hearing by the word of God

questions.text: How does the quotation about Israel at the end of the chapter describe the people?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:21 says that about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.”

answers.text: Zealous and wise
Poor and hungry
Disobedient and contrary
Scattered and few
